categories.name: Vocabulary
categories.intro: Words that show up far more often in AI output than in human writing. One is a coincidence; three in a paragraph is a pattern.

patterns.name: Delve and friends
patterns.description: delve, dive into, deep dive, unpack, explore (for "discuss").
patterns.bad: "Let's delve into the data."
patterns.better: "Here is what the data shows."

patterns.name: Tapestry words
patterns.description: tapestry, landscape, realm, sphere, ecosystem, fabric (used abstractly).
patterns.bad: "the ever-evolving landscape of marketing."
patterns.better: "marketing in 2026" or name the actual change.

patterns.name: Testament and beacon
patterns.description: testament to, beacon of, embodiment of, hallmark of.
patterns.bad: "The launch is a testament to the team's dedication."
patterns.better: "The team shipped it in six weeks."

patterns.name: Pivotal and crucial
patterns.description: pivotal, crucial, vital, paramount, critical (as decoration).
patterns.bad: "plays a pivotal role in growth."
patterns.better: "drives 40% of signups."

patterns.name: Showcase verbs
patterns.description: showcase, highlight, underscore, emphasize, spotlight (as commentary verbs).
patterns.bad: "The results underscore the importance of testing."
patterns.better: "Testing caught three bugs before launch."

patterns.name: Foster and cultivate
patterns.description: foster, cultivate, nurture (applied to abstract things).
patterns.bad: "fostering a culture of innovation."
patterns.better: Say what the team actually does.

patterns.name: Leverage and utilize
patterns.description: leverage, utilize, harness, capitalize on.
patterns.bad: "Leverage AI to streamline your workflow."
patterns.better: "Use AI to draft the weekly report."

patterns.name: Elevate and enhance
patterns.description: elevate, enhance, empower, supercharge, unlock, amplify.
patterns.bad: "Elevate your content strategy."
patterns.better: Name the result: "Post three times a week without writing on weekends."

patterns.name: Seamless and robust
patterns.description: seamless, robust, cutting-edge, state-of-the-art, best-in-class, world-class.
patterns.bad: "a seamless, robust solution."
patterns.better: "it syncs in under a second and hasn't gone down this year."

patterns.name: Intricate and multifaceted
patterns.description: intricate, multifaceted, nuanced, complex (as filler).
patterns.bad: "the intricate interplay of factors."
patterns.better: Name two of the factors.

patterns.name: Meticulous
patterns.description: meticulous, meticulously, painstakingly, carefully crafted.
patterns.bad: "meticulously crafted templates."
patterns.better: "templates tested on 200 posts."

patterns.name: Vibrant and rich
patterns.description: vibrant, rich, bustling, thriving, dynamic.
patterns.bad: "a vibrant community of creators."
patterns.better: "4,000 creators who post weekly."

patterns.name: Journey and embark
patterns.description: journey, embark, navigate, voyage, path (for ordinary processes).
patterns.bad: "embark on your SEO journey."
patterns.better: "start with your top ten pages."

patterns.name: Game changer
patterns.description: game changer, revolutionary, groundbreaking, transformative, paradigm shift.
patterns.bad: "This feature is a game changer."
patterns.better: Say what changes and for whom.

patterns.name: Transition adverbs
patterns.description: Additionally, Furthermore, Moreover, Notably, Importantly (opening sentences).
patterns.bad: "Additionally, the tool supports exports."
patterns.better: "It also exports to CSV."

patterns.name: Empty intensifiers
patterns.description: truly, incredibly, deeply, profoundly, remarkably, fundamentally.
patterns.bad: "a truly remarkable result."
patterns.better: Give the number that makes it remarkable.

patterns.name: Quietly
patterns.description: quietly, silently, subtly (adding drama to plain events).
patterns.bad: "Costs quietly crept up."
patterns.better: "Costs rose 12% in March."

patterns.name: Align and resonate
patterns.description: align with, resonate with, speak to, in line with.
patterns.bad: "content that resonates with your audience."
patterns.better: "posts your audience replies to."

patterns.name: Key as an adjective
patterns.description: key insight, key takeaway, key factor, key role.
patterns.bad: "The key takeaway is consistency."
patterns.better: "Post on the same days every week."

patterns.name: Era words
patterns.description: in today's fast-paced world, in the digital age, in an era of, now more than ever.
patterns.bad: "In today's fast-paced digital world, content is king."
patterns.better: Cut it and start with the point.

patterns.name: I'd be happy to
patterns.description: AI offer openers: I'd be happy to, I'd be delighted to, I'd be thrilled to.
patterns.bad: "I'd be happy to help you with that."
patterns.better: "Here's what I can do."

categories.name: Stock phrases
categories.intro: Ready-made phrases that fill space without adding meaning.

patterns.name: Worth noting
patterns.description: it's worth noting, it's important to note, it should be noted.
patterns.bad: "It's worth noting that the API is rate limited."
patterns.better: "The API allows 100 calls a minute."

patterns.name: At its core
patterns.description: at its core, at the end of the day, when all is said and done, ultimately.
patterns.bad: "At its core, marketing is about people."
patterns.better: Delete, or say something specific about people.

patterns.name: When it comes to
patterns.description: when it comes to, in terms of, with regard to, in the world of.
patterns.bad: "When it comes to scheduling, timing matters."
patterns.better: "Posts at 9am get more reach than posts at 3pm."

patterns.name: Let's dive in
patterns.description: let's dive in, let's get started, buckle up, without further ado.
patterns.bad: "Ready? Let's dive in!"
patterns.better: Start with the first point.

patterns.name: Plays a role
patterns.description: plays a role in, contributes to, is a factor in.
patterns.bad: "Hashtags play a role in reach."
patterns.better: "Posts with 3 to 5 hashtags reached more people in our test."

patterns.name: Stands as
patterns.description: stands as, serves as, functions as, acts as (instead of "is").
patterns.bad: "The dashboard serves as a central hub."
patterns.better: "The dashboard shows every scheduled post."

patterns.name: Navigate the complexities
patterns.description: navigate the complexities of, the ins and outs of, the nuances of.
patterns.bad: "helping you navigate the complexities of SEO."
patterns.better: "explains how Google picks which page to rank."

patterns.name: Whether you're X or Y
patterns.description: Whether you're a beginner or a pro, from startups to enterprises.
patterns.bad: "Whether you're a solo creator or a global brand, ..."
patterns.better: Say who it is actually for.

patterns.name: Look no further
patterns.description: look no further, you've come to the right place, this is your ultimate guide.
patterns.bad: "Looking for a scheduler? Look no further."
patterns.better: "FeedHive schedules posts to 10 platforms."

patterns.name: Unlock the power
patterns.description: unlock the power of, harness the potential of, take it to the next level.
patterns.bad: "Unlock the full potential of your content."
patterns.better: Say the specific gain.

patterns.name: Here's the thing
patterns.description: here's the thing, here's the deal, let me be clear, I'll be honest, I'll be straight with you.
patterns.bad: "Here's the thing: most people quit."
patterns.better: "Most people quit in month two."

patterns.name: The truth is
patterns.description: the truth is, the reality is, the uncomfortable truth, the hard truth.
patterns.bad: "The hard truth is that SEO takes time."
patterns.better: "SEO takes about six months to show results."

patterns.name: Sign-off clichés
patterns.description: I hope this helps, happy writing, feel free to reach out, let me know if you have any questions.
patterns.bad: A post or article ending with "Hope this helps!"
patterns.better: End on the last useful point.

patterns.name: Summary openers
patterns.description: In conclusion, In summary, To sum up, Overall, All in all.
patterns.bad: "In conclusion, consistency is key."
patterns.better: End on the last concrete point; the reader was just there.

patterns.name: Vague future
patterns.description: the future is bright, the possibilities are endless, only time will tell, the sky's the limit.
patterns.bad: "With AI, the possibilities are endless."
patterns.better: Name one thing that is now possible.

patterns.name: Feel free to
patterns.description: feel free to reach out, feel free to ask, feel free to share (as filler, not just sign-off).
patterns.bad: "Feel free to reach out if you have any questions."
patterns.better: "Email me if something breaks."

patterns.name: Keep in mind
patterns.description: keep in mind, bear in mind, it's worth remembering (hedge phrases AI overuses).
patterns.bad: "Keep in mind that results may vary."
patterns.better: "Results varied by 12% in our test."

patterns.name: Needless to say
patterns.description: needless to say, it goes without saying, as you may know (filler transitions).
patterns.bad: "Needless to say, consistency is important."
patterns.better: "Consistency matters."

patterns.name: As a [role]
patterns.description: AI self-identification to borrow authority: As a marketing professional, As an expert in.
patterns.bad: "As a marketing professional, I can tell you that..."
patterns.better: "We tested this on 40 accounts. Here's what happened."

categories.name: Sentence patterns
categories.intro: Constructions that AI reaches for again and again.

patterns.name: Not X, but Y
patterns.description: "It's not X. It's Y." / "This isn't about X, it's about Y."
patterns.bad: "It's not a tool. It's a teammate."
patterns.better: Say what it does: "It drafts replies for you to approve."

patterns.name: Not just X, but also Y
patterns.description: "It's not just fast, it's also accurate."
patterns.bad: "Not just a scheduler, but a full content engine."
patterns.better: List what it does.

patterns.name: The question isn't X
patterns.description: "The question isn't whether, it's when." / "The problem isn't X. The problem is Y."
patterns.bad: "The question isn't if you should use AI. It's how."
patterns.better: "Here is how we use AI for first drafts."

patterns.name: Negative listing
patterns.description: "Not a X. Not a Y. A Z."
patterns.bad: "Not a plan. Not a hope. A system."
patterns.better: "A system: three posts a week, written on Mondays."

patterns.name: Rhetorical Q and A
patterns.description: A question the writer immediately answers.
patterns.bad: "Why does this matter? Because reach is everything."
patterns.better: "Reach decides how many people see the post."

patterns.name: The obvious question
patterns.description: "The obvious question is...", "You might be wondering..."
patterns.bad: "You might be wondering how this works."
patterns.better: Explain how it works.

patterns.name: Colon reveal
patterns.description: A short setup, a colon, then a dramatic reveal.
patterns.bad: "The best part: it's free."
patterns.better: "It's free."

patterns.name: Faux insight
patterns.description: "What nobody tells you", "the part most people miss", "here's what most get wrong".
patterns.bad: "What nobody tells you about growth: distribution beats product."
patterns.better: "Distribution brought us more users than any feature."

patterns.name: This is where it gets interesting
patterns.description: this is where it gets interesting, this changes everything, and that's where things get wild.
patterns.bad: "And this is where it gets interesting."
patterns.better: State the interesting thing.

patterns.name: The useful part is
patterns.description: the useful part, the part where, the best part, the exciting part, the part that stuck with me.
patterns.bad: "The useful part is that it connects to your inbox."
patterns.better: "It connects to your inbox."

patterns.name: X is just Y
patterns.description: Calling something "just" a vivid unrelated thing to make a point.
patterns.bad: "Posting without a plan is just gambling with your time."
patterns.better: "Without a plan you post less and repeat topics."

patterns.name: Trailing -ing analysis
patterns.description: A sentence ends with an -ing clause that tells you what it means.
patterns.bad: "Sales rose 20%, highlighting the strength of the brand."
patterns.better: "Sales rose 20%."

patterns.name: Rule of three
patterns.description: Lists of exactly three adjectives or phrases, by reflex.
patterns.bad: "fast, simple, and powerful."
patterns.better: Keep the one that is true and provable.

patterns.name: Synonym cycling
patterns.description: Rotating names for the same thing to avoid repetition.
patterns.bad: "The agent drafts. The assistant reviews. The tool publishes."
patterns.better: "The agent drafts, reviews and publishes."

patterns.name: Arbitrary "one"
patterns.description: Putting "one" before a noun to sound focused when the number means nothing.
patterns.bad: "Start with one workflow."
patterns.better: "Start with your weekly newsletter."

patterns.name: Fake-strong verbs
patterns.description: boasts, features, offers, maintains (instead of "has").
patterns.bad: "The app boasts an intuitive interface."
patterns.better: "The app has a drag-and-drop calendar."

patterns.name: Imagine a world
patterns.description: imagine a world where, picture this, what if I told you.
patterns.bad: "Imagine a world where your posts write themselves."
patterns.better: Describe what the product does today.

patterns.name: Hedge stacking
patterns.description: may potentially, could possibly, might help to, can sometimes.
patterns.bad: "This may potentially help improve results."
patterns.better: "This improved reply rate by 8% in our test." Or cut it.

patterns.name: Both-sides filler
patterns.description: "While X has benefits, it also has drawbacks."
patterns.bad: "While automation saves time, it's important to stay authentic."
patterns.better: Take a position and support it.

patterns.name: From X to Y range
patterns.description: "From startups to enterprises", "from strategy to execution".
patterns.bad: "From ideation to publication, we've got you covered."
patterns.better: Name the two steps you actually handle.

patterns.name: Interpretive asides
patterns.description: Telling the reader how to read the text.
patterns.bad: "That last point matters more than it sounds."
patterns.better: Show why it matters, or delete the aside.

patterns.name: Rhetorical self-correction
patterns.description: "Actually, let me rephrase that", "Or rather..."
patterns.bad: "It's fast. Or rather, it's instant."
patterns.better: "It's instant."

patterns.name: If you've ever...
patterns.description: False familiarity setup: If you've ever wondered, If you've ever struggled with.
patterns.bad: "If you've ever struggled with writer's block, this is for you."
patterns.better: "This helps when you can't think of what to post."

patterns.name: Sound familiar?
patterns.description: Rhetorical resonance device: Sound familiar?, Ring a bell?, You know the feeling?
patterns.bad: "Deadlines, pressure, no time to think. Sound familiar?"
patterns.better: "Most teams don't have time to write posts."

categories.name: Structure and rhythm
categories.intro: Slop is often in the shape of the text, not the words.

patterns.name: One-line paragraph stacks
patterns.description: Many short lines in a row, each a slogan.
patterns.bad: "I quit my job. / I built a product. / Nobody came. / Then I learned this."
patterns.better: Write it as one paragraph.

patterns.name: Fragment drumbeat
patterns.description: Strings of fragments for rhythm.
patterns.bad: "Code. Content. Customers. Every day."
patterns.better: One full sentence that says what you do every day.

patterns.name: Repeated starters
patterns.description: Several lines that start with the same word or phrase.
patterns.bad: "It saves time. It saves money. It saves your sanity."
patterns.better: "It saves about four hours a week."

patterns.name: Identical sentence shapes
patterns.description: Every sentence the same length and structure.
patterns.bad: A paragraph of 12-word sentences, each "Subject verb object, comma, clause."
patterns.better: Vary length when it helps the point.

patterns.name: List dumps
patterns.description: Long inventories of nouns in one breath.
patterns.bad: "sales, marketing, support, ops, finance, hiring, legal and product."
patterns.better: Pick the two that matter here.

patterns.name: Bullets for everything
patterns.description: Bullet points where two sentences of prose would read better.
patterns.bad: Three bullets of four words each.
patterns.better: One sentence.

patterns.name: Headings on tiny sections
patterns.description: Headers over one or two sentences.
patterns.bad: "## Why it matters" followed by one line.
patterns.better: Fold it into the paragraph above.

patterns.name: Recap ending
patterns.description: A final paragraph that repeats the whole piece.
patterns.bad: "To recap, we covered A, B and C."
patterns.better: End on the last point or the next action.

patterns.name: Mic-drop ending
patterns.description: A final "deep" one-liner.
patterns.bad: "The future isn't coming. It's already here."
patterns.better: End on the clearest concrete sentence.

patterns.name: Challenges and future outlook
patterns.description: A formulaic "Despite challenges, the future looks promising" closer.
patterns.bad: "Despite these challenges, the outlook remains positive."
patterns.better: Name the challenge and what is being done.

patterns.name: Fake-unscripted scaffolding
patterns.description: "And honestly...", "And look...", "So yeah..." used as filler.
patterns.bad: "And honestly? That's when it clicked."
patterns.better: Say what clicked.

patterns.name: Over-structured short answers
patterns.description: A short reply split into sections with headers and bold labels.
patterns.bad: A three-sentence answer with "Overview", "Key Points" and "Conclusion".
patterns.better: Three sentences.

categories.name: Imagery and metaphor
categories.intro: AI likes making things vivid when they should be clear.

patterns.name: Cute metaphors
patterns.description: Abstract things doing human or physical actions.
patterns.bad: "Your data is whispering insights."
patterns.better: "Your data shows Tuesday posts get more replies."

patterns.name: Things that "live" or "sit"
patterns.description: Data, products or agents that live or sit somewhere.
patterns.bad: "where your customer data lives."
patterns.better: "where your customer data is stored."

patterns.name: Honest dashboards
patterns.description: Systems that "get honest", "tell the truth", "hide" or "reveal".
patterns.bad: "Analytics finally get honest."
patterns.better: "Analytics now count only real views."

patterns.name: Mixed and stacked metaphors
patterns.description: Two or three images in one sentence.
patterns.bad: "a north star that fuels the engine of growth."
patterns.better: Drop both images and say what drives growth.

patterns.name: Fuel and engine
patterns.description: fuel, engine, rocket, catalyst, springboard, flywheel (as decoration).
patterns.bad: "content that fuels your growth engine."
patterns.better: "posts that bring in signups."

patterns.name: Secret sauce
patterns.description: secret sauce, magic, silver bullet, holy grail.
patterns.bad: "Consistency is the secret sauce."
patterns.better: "Accounts that posted weekly grew twice as fast."

categories.name: Substance
categories.intro: The deepest kind of slop: text that sounds informative and says nothing.

patterns.name: Importance puffery
patterns.description: Inflating significance: "marks a pivotal moment", "a significant shift".
patterns.bad: "This marks a pivotal moment for the industry."
patterns.better: State the fact and let the reader judge.

patterns.name: Vague attribution
patterns.description: experts agree, studies show, many believe, it is widely regarded.
patterns.bad: "Studies show posting daily works."
patterns.better: Name the study, or cut the claim.

patterns.name: Generic claims without receipts
patterns.description: Claims any company could make.
patterns.bad: "AI can transform your business."
patterns.better: "Our AI drafts a week of posts from a 3-line brief."

patterns.name: The portability test
patterns.description: A sentence that could move unchanged to another company or topic.
patterns.bad: "We're committed to delivering value to our customers."
patterns.better: A sentence only you could write.

patterns.name: Fake-profound wisdom
patterns.description: Lines that sound deep and mean nothing concrete.
patterns.bad: "Growth is a mindset, not a metric."
patterns.better: Say what you measure and why.

patterns.name: Smoothing the specific
patterns.description: Replacing a sharp fact with a generic description.
patterns.bad: "a leading expert in the field."
patterns.better: "who wrote the Kubernetes scheduler."

patterns.name: Made-up specifics
patterns.description: Invented numbers, names or examples presented as real.
patterns.bad: "Sarah, a marketing manager, saved 10 hours a week." (no Sarah exists)
patterns.better: A real example, or none.

patterns.name: Telling instead of showing
patterns.description: Labeling something surprising, important or interesting.
patterns.bad: "Surprisingly, the simple version won."
patterns.better: "The simple version got twice the clicks."

patterns.name: Canned notability
patterns.description: "featured in top outlets", "widely recognized", "has an active social media presence".
patterns.bad: "She has been featured in numerous leading publications."
patterns.better: Name one, with a link.

patterns.name: Superficial balance
patterns.description: Every point gets a "however" so the text never commits.
patterns.bad: "AI is powerful. However, it has limitations."
patterns.better: Say which limitation matters for this reader.

patterns.name: Advice with no steps
patterns.description: Telling the reader to "optimize", "be strategic" or "stay consistent" without saying how.
patterns.bad: "Optimize your posting schedule."
patterns.better: "Post Tuesday to Thursday between 8 and 10am."

patterns.name: Hollow promises
patterns.description: "Everything you need to know", "the ultimate guide", "master X in minutes".
patterns.bad: "The ultimate guide to LinkedIn."
patterns.better: "How to write a LinkedIn post that gets replies."

patterns.name: Em dash habit
patterns.description: Em dashes used everywhere for rhythm.
patterns.bad: "It's fast — really fast — and free."
patterns.better: "It's fast and free." Use commas, periods or parentheses.

patterns.name: Bold sprinkled mid-sentence
patterns.description: Random words in bold for emphasis.
patterns.bad: "This is **really important** for **growth**."
patterns.better: No bold; let the sentence carry it.

patterns.name: Emoji as bullets
patterns.description: ✅ 🚀 💡 👉 used as list markers or decoration.
patterns.bad: "✅ Faster ✅ Cheaper ✅ Better"
patterns.better: A plain sentence.

patterns.name: Title Case Headings
patterns.description: Every Word Capitalized In Headings.
patterns.bad: "How To Grow Your Audience On LinkedIn"
patterns.better: "How to grow your audience on LinkedIn"

patterns.name: Colon-label lines
patterns.description: Every line starts with a bold label and a colon.
patterns.bad: "**Speed:** fast. **Price:** low. **Support:** great."
patterns.better: A sentence about the one that matters.

patterns.name: Markdown in the wrong place
patterns.description: Asterisks, hashtags or headers pasted into emails, posts or forms.
patterns.bad: "**Subject:** ..." inside a LinkedIn post.
patterns.better: Plain text.

patterns.name: Curly-quote and character mix
patterns.description: Curly quotes, special dashes and non-breaking spaces mixed with plain text.
patterns.bad: “quotes” next to "quotes" in one paragraph.
patterns.better: Pick one style.

patterns.name: Exclamation inflation
patterns.description: Exclamation marks on ordinary sentences.
patterns.bad: "We updated the settings page!"
patterns.better: "We updated the settings page."

patterns.name: Unicode bold and fancy fonts in long posts
patterns.description: 𝗕𝗼𝗹𝗱 or 𝓈𝒸𝓇𝒾𝓅𝓉 letters across whole lines.
patterns.bad: An entire LinkedIn post in Unicode bold.
patterns.better: Plain text, one bold phrase at most (screen readers can't read these).

patterns.name: Tables for two facts
patterns.description: A table where a sentence would do.
patterns.bad: A 2x2 table comparing price and speed.
patterns.better: "A is cheaper; B is faster."

categories.name: Chatbot residue
categories.intro: Text that was clearly copied out of a chat window.

patterns.name: Assistant openers
patterns.description: Certainly!, Absolutely!, Great question!, Of course!
patterns.bad: "Certainly! Here's a LinkedIn post about..."
patterns.better: Delete it.

patterns.name: Sycophancy
patterns.description: You're absolutely right, what a great idea, I love this.
patterns.bad: An email reply starting "Great point, you're absolutely right!"
patterns.better: Answer the point.

patterns.name: Offer to do more
patterns.description: Would you like me to..., Let me know if you'd like a shorter version.
patterns.bad: A published post ending "Would you like me to adjust the tone?"
patterns.better: Delete it.

patterns.name: Here is a...
patterns.description: Lead-ins like "Here is a polished version of your post:" left in the final text.
patterns.better: Delete the line.

patterns.name: Placeholder text
patterns.description: [Your Name], [Company], [insert statistic], XX%.
patterns.better: Fill it in or cut the sentence.

patterns.name: AI disclaimers
patterns.description: As an AI, I don't have personal opinions; my knowledge is limited to...
patterns.better: Delete it.

patterns.name: Source hedging
patterns.description: "Based on available information", "specific details are limited".
patterns.bad: "While specific figures are not widely available, ..."
patterns.better: Find the figure or don't mention it.

patterns.name: Citation debris
patterns.description: Leftover markers like [1], contentReference, oaicite, turn0search0.
patterns.better: Remove them, and check the claim they were attached to.

patterns.name: Happy to help!
patterns.description: Standalone AI closer: Happy to help!, Glad I could help!, Happy to assist!
patterns.bad: "Let me know if you need anything else. Happy to help!"
patterns.better: "Let me know if you need anything else."

patterns.name: I'm here to help
patterns.description: AI availability assertion: I'm here to help, I'm here to assist, Don't hesitate to ask.
patterns.bad: "I'm here to help if you need anything."
patterns.better: Delete it. The work speaks for itself.

categories.name: Social media and LinkedIn
categories.intro: Patterns that turn a post into "LinkedIn slop".

patterns.name: Broetry
patterns.description: One sentence per line, top to bottom.
patterns.bad: A 20-line post where every line is a new sentence.
patterns.better: Short paragraphs.

patterns.name: Hook formulas
patterns.description: "I was fired. Best thing that ever happened.", "Unpopular opinion:", "Stop doing X."
patterns.better: Open with the specific thing that happened or the specific claim.

patterns.name: Thrilled to announce
patterns.description: I'm thrilled/excited/humbled to announce, I'm proud to share.
patterns.bad: "I'm thrilled to announce I've joined Acme!"
patterns.better: "I joined Acme to lead the growth team."

patterns.name: Read that again
patterns.description: Read that again., Let that sink in., I'll say it louder.
patterns.better: Delete it. If the line needs a second read, rewrite it.

patterns.name: Agree? / Thoughts?
patterns.description: Engagement-bait closers.
patterns.bad: "Agree? 👇"
patterns.better: Ask a real question, or don't.

patterns.name: The lesson list
patterns.description: "Here are 7 lessons I learned from..." with generic lessons.
patterns.better: One lesson with the story behind it.

patterns.name: Humblebrag setup
patterns.description: "I don't usually post this, but...", "This might be controversial, but..."
patterns.better: Post it without the preamble.

patterns.name: Thread markers
patterns.description: 🧵, 1/, "A thread" on content that isn't a thread.
patterns.better: Write the post.

patterns.name: Hashtag walls
patterns.description: Ten or more hashtags at the end.
patterns.better: Three relevant ones, or none.

patterns.name: That's it. That's the post
patterns.description: Self-aware closers that announce the ending.
patterns.bad: "That's it. That's the tweet."
patterns.better: Just stop.

patterns.name: P.S. engagement
patterns.description: "P.S. Repost ♻️ if this helped." on every post.
patterns.better: Drop it, or use it rarely.

patterns.name: No fluff, just value
patterns.description: Announcing quality instead of delivering it: no fluff, just value; straight to the point; real talk.
patterns.better: Delete the announcement.

patterns.name: Comment slop
patterns.description: Generic replies: "Great insights!", "So true!", "Thanks for sharing, this is gold."
patterns.better: Reply to something specific in the post, or don't reply.

patterns.name: Fake vulnerability arc
patterns.description: "I failed. I was broke. Then I discovered X." built to sell.
patterns.better: Tell what happened, with dates and numbers.

patterns.name: Contrarian template
patterns.description: "Everyone says X. They're wrong."
patterns.better: Make your claim and back it up; skip the strawman.
